title: Where does a tree get its mass?
promise: Explain how carbon from air becomes a major part of a tree’s dry mass.

scenes.narration: A tree grows heavier each year. But much of its dry mass begins as an invisible gas in the air, not as soil.
scenes.visual: Open with a tree silhouette, then isolate the question of dry mass.

scenes.narration: Leaves take in carbon dioxide. Roots supply water. Light energy powers reactions that let plants build organic molecules.
scenes.visual: Construct labelled input arrows for carbon dioxide, water and light.

scenes.narration: Photosynthesis incorporates carbon into sugars. The plant uses these molecules as fuel and as building blocks for growth.
scenes.visual: Trace carbon into a sugar unit; distinguish energy from matter.

scenes.narration: Wood contains carbon that came from carbon dioxide. Water contributes much fresh mass, while minerals remain essential in smaller amounts.
scenes.visual: Build a trunk from linked carbon units; retain a mineral side note.
